defect.evidence_quote: The 911 caller in this case reported more than a minor traffic infraction and more than a conclusory allegation of drunk or reckless driving. Instead, she alleged a specific and dangerous result of the driver’s conduct: running another car off the highway.
defect.problem: The holding is supportable only if narrowed. The opinion did not endorse any 911 report of dangerous/reckless driving; it stressed a specific report that the caller was run off the road, with reliability indicia, creating reasonable suspicion of drunk driving.
defect.proposed_fix: A 911 call reporting that a specifically identified vehicle ran the caller off the road can, under the totality of the circumstances, supply reasonable suspicion of drunk driving when the call bears adequate indicia of reliability.

reasons: The opinion says the stop complied because the officer had reasonable suspicion that the driver was intoxicated.
The Court found the call reliable based on eyewitness knowledge, near-contemporaneous reporting, and use of the 911 system.
The broader phrase dangerous/reckless driving risks exceeding the Court's own limitation that not all traffic infractions imply intoxication.
residual_risks: The lake record has no separate holding field, so support is verified from the cached opinion text.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Tie the holding to a specific, contemporaneous 911 report that the identified vehicle ran the caller off the road, and to reasonable suspicion of drunk driving.

reasons: The opinion is centrally about whether a 911 tip supplied reasonable suspicion for an investigative traffic stop.
The Court applied and refined the anonymous-tip reliability framework from White and J.L. under the reasonable-suspicion standard.
residual_risks: The role label is editorial rather than a direct holding, but it is grounded in the opinion's repeated reasonable-suspicion analysis.
